moduleTitle: Integrating Testim with Azure DevOps & GitHub Actions for streamlined test results
learningObjectives: Set up a GitHub Actions workflow that installs the Testim CLI and runs tests.
Trigger Testim runs from Azure DevOps release pipelines.
Explain how GitHub branch activity is mirrored into Testim.

elements.description: Configure a GitHub Actions runner with supported Node.js, the Testim CLI, project/grid and protected credentials. Run the CLI and collect its report; a workflow snippet is not proof of a successful integration. The vendor examples contain older runtime/action versions; verify supported current versions before use.

Repository integration is separate from Actions. After connecting the repository and enabling Create/Merge, created branches use the same name but always base on Testim Master, not the GitHub source branch. Merge synchronization occurs on pull-request actions and targets Testim Master; it does not mirror every arbitrary merge or branch hierarchy.

bulletPoints: GitHub Actions: a workflow installs Node.js + the Testim CLI, then runs it as a step.
Configured repository Create/Merge actions have Testim Master-base and PR-merge restrictions.

elements.description: Azure Pipelines can install a supported Node.js runtime and the CLI, execute tests and publish the generated JUnit report. The cited vendor snippet uses obsolete Node 10.x; treat it as a workflow example, not a current runtime recommendation.

elements.text: This is the same underlying pattern as GitHub Actions and Jenkins — the CI/CD tool calls into the Testim CLI/API as a pipeline step — Azure DevOps is just one more platform this generalizes to.

bulletPoints: Azure DevOps release pipelines can trigger Testim runs directly.
Same underlying mechanism generalizes across Jenkins, GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and GitLab CI.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing GitHub Actions integration with GitHub branch integration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Assuming setting up a GitHub Actions workflow automatically also mirrors branches/merges into Testim, or vice versa.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Actions runs the configured CLI workflow. Repository integration separately enables Create/Merge with Master-base and pull-request merge limitations; neither setup automatically configures the other.

practiceQuiz.scenario: What does a GitHub Actions workflow need to set up before it can run Testim tests?

options.text: Nothing — Testim runs natively in GitHub Actions with no setup.

practiceQuiz.hint: Same CLI as everywhere else, so it needs the same runtime.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Integrating Testim with GitHub Actions means creating a workflow with Node.js and installing the Testim CLI — since the CLI is a Node.js/npm package, that runtime is a prerequisite.

optionExplanations.A: The CLI needs a supported Node.js runtime plus actual runner configuration.
optionExplanations.B: A Python-only environment does not supply the npm CLI runtime.
optionExplanations.C: The CLI and runner configuration are not automatically supplied by every workflow.
optionExplanations.D: An Academy account is not the CLI runtime.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A connected repository enables Create and Merge actions. Which describes the documented Testim branch behavior?

options.text: Nothing — GitHub branches have no relationship to Testim branches.
Same-name branches base on Testim Master; pull-request merge actions merge tests into Testim Master.
The entire Testim project is deleted and recreated.
A manual export/import step is required each time.

practiceQuiz.hint: Testim does not preserve every GitHub source-branch base.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The repository integration documents same-name creation from Testim Master and merge synchronization only on PR actions into Master. This is distinct from merely running an Actions workflow.

optionExplanations.A: Configured Create/Merge integration establishes the documented relationship.
optionExplanations.B: This states the documented Master-base and PR-merge restrictions.
optionExplanations.C: Branch synchronization does not delete the entire project.
optionExplanations.D: The configured actions do not require a manual export/import for each event.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which of the following can trigger a Testim run from a release pipeline?

options.text: Azure DevOps, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI.
Only Azure DevOps — no other platform supports this.
Only a manual click inside the Testim editor.
This capability doesn't exist in Testim.

practiceQuiz.hint: It's the same set of major CI/CD platforms named throughout this integrations section.
practiceQuiz.rationale: You can fire Testim runs from Azure DevOps, Jenkins, GitHub Actions, and GitLab CI, triggering them directly from release pipelines rather than needing a manual run.

optionExplanations.A: Configured CI jobs can invoke Testim on these platforms.
optionExplanations.B: The CLI workflow is not Azure-only.
optionExplanations.C: CI invocation need not be a manual editor click.

quickRecap.value: Workflow installs Node.js + Testim CLI, then runs it as a step.
Enable repository actions separately: branches base on Testim Master and PR merges target Master.
Release pipelines can trigger Testim runs directly, same pattern as Jenkins/GitHub Actions/GitLab CI.
